findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Guests commit before calendar updates and invitations, so a subsequent failure strands them while retries reject their already-persisted emails.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The route schema permits empty and duplicate guest lists while the shipped client rejects both, giving non-UI callers a different accepted-input contract.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Repeated new addresses survive uniqueGuests filtering and reach createMany twice, so API callers bypass the dialog's uniqueness validation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Passing the original guests array misclassifies existing attendees in mixed submissions as newly invited and sends them scheduled emails instead of guest-change updates.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — If calendar synchronization rejects after attendee creation, retrying the same guests fails uniqueness checks before synchronization or invitations can recover.
packages/emails/email-manager.ts:529 — Guest notifications ignore disableStandardEmails.all host and attendee settings, sending unwanted standard emails for event types that disable them.
apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — Defining a second guest-email schema in the dialog lets client and API validation drift, producing inconsistent rules across callers.

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:1 — The only consumer is AddGuestsDialog, but this booking-specific control is exported from @calcom/ui while importing @calcom/lib and its own public barrel, creating a circular cross-package boundary that makes the shared UI API harder to change.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — sendAddGuestsEmails repeats the organizer and team-member fan-out in sendLocationChangeEmails, so future changes to booking-update recipients must be maintained in two paths and can drift.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The unbounded guest array is materialized as bulk inserts, a full attendee reload, calendar update, and concurrent email fanout in one request, allowing a large request to exhaust database and mail capacity.
packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — Each attendee checks the entire unbounded newGuests array, making guest additions quadratic and delaying mail dispatch for large events.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Email delivery failures are swallowed after guests are persisted, so callers receive success with no retry path while attendees remain unnotified.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Comparing raw guest addresses against a lowercased blacklist lets attendees bypass blocked recipients by changing email-domain casing and disclose booking details to them.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — No test exercises the organizer, attendee, team-role, and outsider authorization branches, so a permission regression could let unauthorized users modify bookings.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — No test covers case-insensitive existing or blacklisted addresses, so mixed-case input can bypass filtering and add duplicate or forbidden guests.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — No recipient-matrix test covers partially filtered input, so forwarding the original guest list can send existing or blacklisted attendees the wrong email template.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42 — No dialog test covers mutation errors, so the always-truthy interpolated message can expose an undefined code instead of the intended fallback error.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Comparing raw guest addresses against a lowercased blacklist lets attendees bypass blocked recipients by changing email-domain casing and disclose booking details to them.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same security vulnerability as the golden comment. Both point out that in addGuests.handler.ts, the blacklist check compares guest emails against a lowercased blacklist without lowercasing the input guest emails first. The golden comment says 'blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails', and the candidate says 'Comparing raw guest addresses against a lowercased blacklist'. Both identify that this allows bypassing the blacklist by using different casing in the email addresses.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Passing the original guests array misclassifies existing attendees in mixed submissions as newly invited and sends them scheduled emails instead of guest-change updates.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem - that passing the original guests array causes misclassification of attendees when determining who receives AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (which the candidate calls 'guest-change updates'). Both comments point to the same bug where the logic for distinguishing new guests from existing attendees is flawed, leading to incorrect email types being sent. The candidate correctly identifies this happens at the sendAddGuestsEmails call and describes the same consequence (existing attendees being treated as newly invited).

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same problem as the golden comment. Both point out that uniqueGuests filtering does not deduplicate duplicate entries within the input itself, allowing repeated emails to pass through to createMany. The candidate mentions 'Repeated new addresses survive uniqueGuests filtering and reach createMany twice' which is exactly the same issue as 'does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.'

per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - that the sendAddGuestsEmails function (at line 529 in email-manager.ts) does not check/respect the disableStandardEmails flags, which would result in sending emails when they should be disabled. Both comments point to the same bug: guest notification emails ignoring the disableStandardEmails settings in EventType metadata.
